title: Muzumdar Demands Aggressive Cricket as India Open Women's T20 Asia Cup Campaign
excerpt: India's head coach acknowledges the team's poor T20 form in 2026 but says the young squad is hungry for success as they begin a crucial six-month stretch of tournaments.
body:
• India head coach Amol Muzumdar has called on his young squad to play aggressive cricket as they open their Women's T20 Asia Cup campaign against Thailand in Dubai.
  • India have won just seven of 16 T20Is in 2026, including a group-stage exit from the T20 World Cup, but Muzumdar says the team has "huge scope of improvement."
  • Key batter Jemimah Rodrigues is out of the tournament with a high-grade hamstring tear sustained during The Hundred in England.
  • The Asia Cup is the first of three major T20 tournaments for India in six months, followed by the Asian Games in Japan and the Champions Trophy in Sri Lanka.

India women's cricket head coach Amol Muzumdar has acknowledged his team's inconsistent T20 form this year but insists the squad is "hungry for success" as they open their Asia Cup campaign against Thailand in Dubai on Sunday.

Speaking to reporters at the ICC Academy Oval ahead of the tournament opener, Muzumdar outlined an aggressive approach for a team that has struggled in the shortest format in 2026, winning just seven of 16 T20 Internationals — a win-loss ratio of 0.77 that ranks near the bottom among recent T20 World Cup participants.

A Fresh Start After World Cup Disappointment

India were eliminated in the group stage of the Women's T20 World Cup earlier this year, a result that came on the heels of series losses to South Africa (1-4) and England (1-2). The results have raised questions about the team's competitiveness in T20 cricket, even as they have performed well in ODIs and Tests.

"We don't pay too much attention to the form that you are talking about. But at the same time, we know what scope of improvement this team has got. There is a huge scope of improvement. This is a young side. We are trying to play good, aggressive cricket. And from here on, we will try and set the tone for the next six months."

— Amol Muzumdar, India women's head coach

The former Mumbai batting stalwart pointed to India's success in other formats as evidence of the squad's quality. In the last five Tests, India have won four, and the team has been competitive in ODIs. Muzumdar believes that form can translate to the shorter format with the right approach.

Rodrigues Absence Leaves a Gap

India will be without Jemimah Rodrigues, one of their most experienced T20 batters, after she suffered a high-grade right hamstring tear on August 3 while playing for Southern Brave in The Hundred in England. The BCCI has not announced a specific recovery timeline.

Muzumdar called Rodrigues a "clutch player" who will be "definitely missed" but stressed that her recovery takes priority. Pratika Rawal, who has represented India in ODIs but is yet to play a T20I or Women's Premier League match, has been named as her replacement.

Spinners Key in Dubai Conditions

Muzumdar highlighted the role spinners could play in the humid Dubai conditions. India's spin arsenal includes Shree Charani, the world's top-ranked spinner, and veteran all-rounder Deepti Sharma.

"Spinners definitely are crucial. We have got a variety of spinners in this side," Muzumdar said. "In the few training sessions we have had, it was seen that the wickets do tend to help the spinners, which is a good sign for us."

Six Months of High-Stakes Cricket

The Asia Cup is the first of three major T20 tournaments packed into a six-month window for India. After Dubai, they head to Japan in September to defend their gold medal at the Asian Games, followed by the inaugural Women's Champions Trophy in Sri Lanka in February 2027.

India are the most successful team in Women's Asia Cup history, winning seven of nine editions. They finished runners-up in 2024, losing to hosts Sri Lanka by eight wickets in the final. India's group-stage schedule includes matches against Hong Kong on September 3 and Pakistan on September 5 at the Dubai International Stadium.

For Indian cricket fans in the diaspora, the Asia Cup offers a chance to see whether Muzumdar's young squad can rediscover the aggressive, winning cricket that has been missing in T20Is this year.
